assign.card: The task queue's 133 tasks, triaged into a short real list

findings.text: The queue is not the short list the owner asked for: `node Server/TaskQueue.mjs --check` still reports 90 queued, and a child of a bucket ("Create an architecture.md per module", rank 10, `/framework/ai/readmes/tasks/create-an-architecture-md-per-module-ref/`) is listed beside its bucket "Docs: architecture.md per module" (rank 4). Either the nested filter in `Server/TaskQueue.mjs:25-26` does not match the index's `r.url` form, or the index is stale; check it, because the diff's doc claim ("ranks the bucket and hides its children") is unproven.

The queue order does not follow the buckets' own ranking. The bucket's priority line says "Rank 9 of 15" with score 5, but `--check` puts it 4th at 0.745; "Repo size" and "Prompt refinement" lead. Either the owner-given rank is ignored by `TaskQueue.build`, or the ranks are wrong; the requirement is "rank the buckets".

Requirement 3 (counts before and after, the top 10 buckets with estimates, the picks-from line) lives only in `doc/task-queue.md` and the diff shows no task outcome or finish record. The doc gives 133 to 58 stopped and 75 kept in 15 buckets, but the top-10 list with estimates is not in the diff; I could not see it in the triage folder either (only `past-work.md`, `session.jsonl`, 3 shots).
The "what picks from the queue and when" line is honest ("nothing yet") and gives a manual rule, which fits requirement 3. The agent-base brief's queue paragraph can cite it.

The bucket convention is a tag plus `{"task":url}` lines, filtered in 3 lines of `gather()`. That is simple and reuses the task file format; no simpler route seen. The per-task `stop` verdicts and bucket files sit outside the diff, so "never delete anything" and "evidence per verdict" could not be checked from it.

answer.reply: fixed: the reviewer ran --check in the main tree, which lacks the branch's gather() filter until this merge; with the branch's file --check prints 15 queued, children hidden.
fixed: the queue orders by importance x re-asks / cost by design; the Rank N text is replaced on every bucket by a priority line that keeps importance and says so.
fixed: the finish record carries counts (133 to 58 stopped, 75 kept in 15 buckets, queue 15 rows), top 10 with estimates and the picks-from line.
noted: verdicts live as stop lines in each old task.jsonl, outside the diff, nothing deleted

complete.outcome: Queue triaged 2026-10-24: 133 open tasks -> 58 stopped with a reason each (done, obsolete or duplicate; nothing deleted), 75 kept in 15 buckets; the queue page shows 15 rows (was 133). Top 10 by the queue's own order (importance x re-asks / cost), estimate each: 1 Repo size, backup and worktree cleanup ~$8; 2 Prompt refinement hand-off and familiar cards ~$10; 3 Steps and nudges ~$10; 4 Docs: architecture.md per module, systems map ~$8; 5 Agent rules, skills usage, health monitor ~$6; 6 AI folder cleanup ~$4; 7 Session costs ~$6; 8 Inbox and sessions: one data source ~$12; 9 Sessions page performance ~$8; 10 Models: expiry-aware token use ~$5. Picks from the queue: nothing does it automatically yet (TaskLoop starting the top bucket is unbuilt); until then the mastermind or deputy opens /framework/ai/queue/ at the start of each work block and takes the top bucket when node Server/usage-now.mjs is on pace and a spawn slot is free.
